A.explanation: A $1000 \text{ kg}$ car at about $7 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ gives $p = mv \approx 7000 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$, closest to $1 \times 10^4 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$.

B.explanation: This is about 10 times too large and would need a mass near $10000 \text{ kg}$ or a speed near $70 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.

C.explanation: This is about 100 times too large and corresponds to a heavy lorry, not a family car at $25 \text{ km h}^{-1}$.

D.explanation: This is about 1000 times too large and would require an impossibly large mass or speed for a family car.

hints: Start by estimating the two inputs for momentum: a typical family car mass in $\text{kg}$ and the speed $25 \text{ km h}^{-1}$ converted to $\text{m s}^{-1}$.
Recall $p = mv$ and that $25 \text{ km h}^{-1}$ is $25000 \text{ m}$ divided by $3600 \text{ s}$, about $7 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Multiply your estimated mass by about $7 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and decide which power of ten, $10^4$ to $10^7 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$, it is nearest to.
walkthrough: Identify the needed quantities for momentum $p = mv$: estimate the mass $m$ of a family car as about $1000$ to $1500 \text{ kg}$.
Convert the speed to SI units: $v = 25 \text{ km h}^{-1} = 25000 \text{ m} / 3600 \text{ s} \approx 7 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Substitute into $p = mv$: $p \approx 1000 \text{ kg} \times 7 \text{ m s}^{-1} \approx 7000 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$.
Check the order of magnitude: $7000 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$ is $0.7 \times 10^4 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$, so the nearest power-of-ten estimate is $1 \times 10^4 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$.
